static_traits.name: Zhang Lei
static_traits.family_status: Has two children with his wife
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with baseball league teammates strained by negative self-evaluation; has support from wife and children but has not yet shared feelings of inadequacy with them
static_traits.medical_history: Never had similar psychological issues; never received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Able to clearly express distress and emotions, Positive attitude, highly cooperative; tending to use Negative self-evaluation (e.g. 'I am useless''I am not good enough'), prone to focusing on failure and ignoring positive feedback

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling 'useless' and 'not good enough' for performing poorly in my favorite hobby — recreational baseball — these thoughts lead to worthlessness and low self-esteem, and affect mood and daily motivation.
basic_info.core_demands: The impact of these feelings on my self-esteem and daily functioning keeps intensifying, so I hope to improve my view of myself and my baseball performance through counseling, boosting self-esteem and mood. 'I am willing to try anything that can improve how I feel about myself and my baseball skills'.
growth_experiences: After joining a recreational baseball league a few years ago, because of one poor game performance (initially triggered by a bad game, moderate stress), since then repeatedly focusing on failure every time competing or thinking about baseball, ignoring progress, gradually intensifying worthlessness and low self-esteem; relationship with teammates consequently strained, mood and daily Motivation affected; although practicing extra and asking teammates for advice, the sense of inadequacy has not yet eased; has not yet shared such feelings with wife and children.

special_situations.event: Making mistakes in recreational baseball league games (for example, being struck out last week)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not perform well in my favorite hobby, it means I as a person am useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practicing doubly hard and asking teammates for advice to prove oneself, while continuously fixating on mistakes

special_situations.event: After games or when thinking of baseball, focuses only on failures, ignoring good hits or defense
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfection counts as success; anything less than perfect equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive feedback, downplaying good performance to push oneself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those good moments do not matter; I always mess up

special_situations.event: When in contact with teammates or preparing to interact with them, worries about being judged by them
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If teammates see my mistakes, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding teammates, reducing communication to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all laughing at me

special_situations.event: When thinking about whether to share one's feelings of inadequacy with wife and children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I speak these feelings aloud, I will become a burden to my family and be more disgraced
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping Silence, not seeking family support

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, to prove one's own worth (especially in the beloved baseball field)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged, humiliated, and negated as a 'useless person'
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being judged by avoiding exposure and intimate sharing
Maintains a sense of protection against loss of control and shame through self-devaluation and over-practicing

object_relations.object_representation: Picky judges (better teammates who may look down on oneself)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks whether these feelings have been shared with the wife or suggests seeking support from family
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes expressing will burden the family and make oneself more embarrassed (equating sharing with troubling others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Declining to share in a tactful but firm tone, emphasizing 'do not trouble them', avoiding further exploration of shame.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing teammates' feedback or being invited to examine the evidence concretely
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting self-shame and feelings of not being accepted onto teammates, believing they look down on oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using speculative language (e.g. 'they surely think...'), uneasy tone, avoiding concrete facts and positive feedback.

manifestations: Overly tying self-worth to baseball performance; one failure experienced as 'I as a person am useless'; ignoring the fun and bonding meaning of the hobby itself; shame keeping one from sharing inner distress with family
outcomes: Interpersonal avoidance (Relationship tension with teammates, distant sharing with family)

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally meant to be sent outward toward herself instead, restraining making demands of others or expressing, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Saying 'I should not trouble others', not sharing feelings of inadequacy and emotions with wife and children
Turns needed support inward, bearing it alone

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: Believing teammates will look down on oneself and are laughing at oneself
Attributing self-shame to teammates' assumed judgments

positive_force: Has stable family support resources (wife and two children)
A teammate offers encouragement and positive feedback
Keeps practicing and actively seeks teammates' advice
Willing to try cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments (clear motivation to seek help)
negative_force: Self-worth overly attached to baseball performance; black-and-white perfection standards
Mental filtering and negating the positive, persistently focusing on failure
Predicting the future and overgeneralizing, aggravating helplessness
Worries about others' judgment and shame; avoids seeking help from people and family

target_behavior.behavior: Engaging in negative self-talk and Self-deprecation in baseball-related situations (e.g. 'I am useless''I will never get better')
antecedent: Making mistakes in games or performing below Anticipation
Recalling failure moments after the game
Merely thinking about baseball and one's performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Binds self-worth to hobby performance, forming an all-or-nothing perfect standard, driven by cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and mental filtering
target_behavior.function: Escaping the emotions of being judged and shame, gaining short-term sense of control and Self-protection
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, Low mood and decreased motivation; Relationship tension with teammates

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding communication with teammates and seeking support from family
antecedent: Worrying about being judged by teammates or having one's mistakes seen
Shame and worry about 'being a burden' when thinking about sharing feelings of inadequacy with wife and children
target_behavior.core_reason: Shame and Fear of others' judgment; viewing expressing needs as 'troubling others'
target_behavior.function: Escaping possible negative evaluation and Sense of guilt, reducing Anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, Social support not yet utilized, negative emotions persisting and worsening
